touches.text: A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.

A machine the device owns that has settings is reached through its device, with the same help/list/show/get/set: cairn <device> <machine> <command> (eg cairn cairn scheduler list). The bus only ever sees the device, which passes the rest down.
Drives sleep.

Sleep is an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9). Since there is one Cairn in the swarm (5.5.3.8.1), Cairn always starts the sleep token, however many boxes there are. At its time Cairn runs its own sleep routine, then hands the sleep token over the bus to the next device, and so on round the rack in the rack's order (5.7.3.3).
Sleep's base trigger is the clock (2300). Once we can tell how recently things were interacted with, that overrides the clock.
ground_loop (machine): the heartbeat

Beat interval is a setting, 60 s for now, expected to go a lot faster ("faster than once a second") now that nothing heavy hangs off it. So the scheduler fires an entry whose time fell since the last beat, not one that equals the beat's minute: any beat length fires each entry exactly once.
INTENTION:
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.

pulse.py asks nobody anything. It starts the shim if it's down, else tells the mechanisms inside the shim that need a pulse "here ya go!" Only daemon-shaped things hang there, things that actually need a heartbeat (eg cc's Gmail fetch, 10.3.6); everything else fires on events. WHY: "the point behind the ground loop firing pulse.py was to give you a structure to hang deamons from, not managers."
scheduler (part of the base shim; uses tools base, rack)
PURPOSE: Holds each device's list of scheduled things.
WHY: The few timed things in the system hang off the one heartbeat, each on its own device's list, so no device grows a daemon of its own (5.6).
INTENTION:
The pulse triggers the check: each pulse, the shim checks its device's list against the clock. No match, the pulse is dropped; a match is a PROBE that kicks off that thing in the device (5.6.4.6).
Sleep is one entry on Cairn's list (5.3.3.1).
Part of the base shim, so every device can schedule things with it (eg Recovery's weekly SSD check is on Recovery's own list).
COMMANDS: list, show, get, set (2.4.10).

Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."
Daily, in sleep (5.3.3): every proof.
Weekly: what is too long or too host-bound to run daily, such as hollow re-runs of every proof and each box's own run of the proofs it can run.

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).
